title: Risk-adapted treatment for cancer of the immune system
official: RAdICAL: Risk-Adapted Immunochemotherapy to Cure Aggressive Lymphoma
summary:
Background and study aims
Large B-cell Lymphoma refers to a group of aggressive B cell lymphomas including diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) and high-grade B cell lymphoma. Approximately 1 in 3 patients’ lymphoma will either fail to respond (r) to treatment or relapse (r) after an initial response. Current standard treatments for patients are R-CHOP and Pola-R-CHP. Currently available tools are unable to accurately predict which patients are at highest risk of failing to respond or relapsing (r/r).
The RAdICAL trial aims to find out whether new scientific tools can more accurately identify patients at highest risk of r/r LBCL.  The trial will use 4 different tests to do this using extra blood tests, diagnostic tissue biopsy material and PET scans. Participants found to be high-risk from one or more of these tests will receive an additional drug, called Epcoritamab, as well as the standard of care R-CHOP/Pola-RCHP. Participants found to be not high-risk will receive R-CHOP/Pola-RCHP only.

Who can participate?
Patients aged 18-80 years, with Large B-cell lymphoma.

What does the study involve?
All participants will receive one initial cycle of R-CHOP/Pola-RCHP, during which it will be determined if they are in the high-risk group.  Participants determined to be non high-risk will receive treatment every 3 weeks, for 6 cycles in total.  Participants in the high-risk group will attend for the same treatment but will also receive Epcoritamab and 2 additional doses of of Epcoritamab after cycle 6. Participants  will have blood tests and an examination to make sure they are well enough to receive treatment. Participants will have up to 3 PET scans, a CT scan and be followed up for 24 months.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Clinical trials are carefully designed to reduce the risks and increase the benefits to all participants. However, we cannot guarantee that participants will have any specific treatment benefits when taking part in a trial. We also cannot guarantee to participants that there are no risks involved when taking part in a trial.
Possible benefits:
·	The trial treatment may improve the chance of your lymphoma going into remission and increase the chance of staying in remission.
·	You will be helping to further our knowledge of how to treat cancer and this will benefit society and others with the same condition in the future
Possible risks/disadvantages:
·	The trial treatment may not provide additional benefit to standard treatment
·	There may be additional risks or side effects (further information can be found in the Patient Information Sheet)
·	You will need to attend more clinic visits, provide more blood samples and have some additional scans than if you were not taking part in the trial.
·	There could be risks to your child if you, or your partner, become pregnant, or begin breastfeeding (further information can be found in the Patient Information Sheet)

Where is the study run from?
University of Southampton (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
September 2026 to June 2030

Who is funding the study?
Genmab (Denmark)
AbbVie (USA)

Who is the main contact?
radical@soton.ac.uk

interventions.name: Tepkinly [epcoritamab], MabThera [rituximab], cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisolone, polatuzumab vedotin

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Histologically confirmed LBCL, expressing CD20. Sufficient diagnostic material must be available to send to HMDS for gene expression profiling and central pathology review. The following diagnoses by the 2016 WHO classification of lymphoid neoplasms may be included:
1.1.	DLBCL, not otherwise specified (NOS) 
1.2.	T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma
1.3.	High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements (double-hit or triple-hit lymphoma)
1.4.	High-grade B-cell lymphoma, NOS
1.5.	LBCL arising from underlying indolent lymphoma (marginal zone or follicular sub-types) where the indolent lymphoma has been exclusively under observation and not previously treated
2.	FDG-avid assessable disease
3.	Not previously treated for lymphoma and intended for treatment with 6 cycles of RCHOP/Pola-RCHP with curative intent
4.	Participants must have an ECOG performance status of 0-2 prior to initiating treatment. Participants with an ECOG ≥3 may be screened if pre-phase treatment is planned. Subject may be eligible if ECOG performance status were to improve to 0-2 after pre-phase treatment. 
5.	Haemoglobin ≥8.0 g/dL (red cell transfusion permitted)
6.	Adequate bone marrow function with platelets >75x10^9/L; neutrophils >1.0x10^9/L at study entry
7.	Measured or calculated creatinine clearance > 40mls/min, (calculated using the formula of Cockcroft and Gault [(140-Age) x Mass (kg) x (1.04 (for women) or 1.23 (for men))/Serum Creatinine (µmolL)])
8.	Serum bilirubin <1.5 x the upper limit of normal and transaminases <2.5 x the upper limit of normal at the time of study entry
9.	Cardiac function sufficient to tolerate 300mg/m² of doxorubicin
a.	No formal assessment of LVEF function is required if the 12-lead ECG is normal and there is no cardiac history
b.	If the 12-lead ECG is not normal or there is a history of cardiac morbidity, a pre-treatment echocardiogram or MUGA is required to establish a baseline ≥50% LVEF equal to or greater than the institutional normal range
10.	No concurrent uncontrolled medical condition that would preclude treatment with R-CHOP/Pola-RCHP
11.	Aged ≥ 18 years old and < 80 years old
12.	Ability to understand the purpose and risks of the study and provide signed and dated informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Participants who have received immunisation with a live vaccine within four weeks prior to enrolment will be ineligible
2.	Diagnosis of primary mediastinal lymphoma
3.	Diagnosis of primary Central Nervous System lymphoma or secondary CNS involvement. Those participants presenting with neurological symptoms should be investigated for CNS involvement. Routine CNS imaging or diagnostic lumbar puncture will not be required in the absence of symptoms
4.	Seizure disorder requiring anti-epileptic therapy unless well-controlled and seizure-free for >12 months
5.	Active significant infection (e.g. progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), tuberculosis, sepsis, and opportunistic infections)
6.	Uncontrolled autoimmune haemolytic anaemia (AIHA) or idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP)
7.	Participants with pre-existing peripheral neuropathy ≥ grade 2
8.	Major surgery in the 2 weeks prior to enrolment. If a participant has undergone recent major surgery >2 weeks ago, they must have recovered adequately from the surgery and any complications before the first dose of Epcoritamab
9.	Corticosteroid use >10 mg day of prednisolone or equivalent, for purposes other than lymphoma symptom control
If glucocorticoid treatment is urgently required for lymphoma symptom control prior to the start of study treatment, prednisone 100 mg or equivalent could be given for a maximum of 72 hours prior to PET scan and ctDNA collection
10.	No clinically significant cardiovascular disease, including:
10.1.	Myocardial infarction or stroke within 6 months prior to study entry
10.2.	Unstable or uncontrolled disease/condition related to or affecting cardiac function (e.g. unstable angina, congestive heart failure, New York Heart Association Class III-IV), uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia within the last 3 months
10.3.	Screening 12-lead ECG showing a baseline QT interval as corrected by Fredericia’s formula (QTcF) >470 msec (Male) or >480 msec (female)
10.4.	Other clinically significant ECG abnormalities within 6 months prior to enrolment unless deemed stable and appropriately treated 
11.	Participants with a history of treatment for tuberculosis (TB) in the past 12 months and participants with latent TB must initiate treatment for latent TB before enrolment into the study
12.	Serological positivity for Hepatitis B, C, or known HIV infection. As per standard of care, prior to initiation of immunochemotherapy, the results of hepatitis serology should be known prior to commencement of therapy.
12.1.	Positive test results for chronic HBV infection (defined as positive HBsAg serology) will not be eligible. Participants with occult or prior HBV infection (defined as negative HBsAg and positive total HBcAb) may be included if HBV DNA is negative, if they are willing to undergo HBV DNA PCR testing, and prescribed HBV prophylaxis. Participants who have protective titres of hepatitis B surface antibody (HBsAb) after vaccination will be eligible. 
12.2.	Participants positive for HCV antibody are eligible only if polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is negative for HCV RNA.
13.	Women who can bear children must agree to use one highly effective form of contraception with an additional barrier or abstinence during the study and for 12 months after the last treatment dose. 
14.	Breastfeeding or pregnant women
15.	Men who can father children must agree to use one highly effective form of contraception with an additional barrier or abstinence during the study and for 12 months after the last treatment dose.  
16.	Men must agree to refrain from sperm donation during the study and for 12 months after the last treatment dose
17.	Serious medical or psychiatric illness likely to affect participation or that may compromise the ability to give informed consent
18.	History of other malignancy that could affect compliance with the protocol or interpretation of results:
18.1.	Participants with a history of curatively treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, or in situ carcinoma of the cervix at any time prior to the study are eligible
18.2.	Participants with low-grade, early-stage prostate cancer (Gleason score 6 or below, Stage 1 or 2) with no requirement for therapy at any time prior to the study are eligible
18.3.	Participants receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy for non-metastatic, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer for 2 or more years prior to enrolment are eligible
18.4.	Participants with any other malignancy treated with curative intent and in remission without treatment for 2 years prior to enrolment are eligible
19.	Any immunotherapy within 4 weeks of the 1st dose of the study
20.	Concurrent participation in another therapeutic clinical trial
21.	History of clinically significant pneumonitis
